items.title: Almost no real-patient evidence
items.whyItMatters: Only one retrieved study compared app advice with clinician triage for the same real people (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Ask each company for a real-user comparison of the listed version.

items.title: Accuracy drifts between versions
items.whyItMatters: Published figures may not describe the version that would be listed (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Tie any listing to a version with re-testing after major updates.

items.title: Groups served worse
items.whyItMatters: Older callers, infants with fever and people with limited English received less accurate advice.
items.opportunity: Report accuracy for these groups separately and ask the companies for it.

items.title: Vignettes overstate accuracy
items.whyItMatters: Lay wording lowers accuracy by 12 points (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Present vignette and real-user results separately to the committee.

errorsFound: A figure of 95 percent for correct emergency advice circulates informally; no retrieved record supports it.
reevaluation: The review should lead with the absence of real-user evidence and give the committee concrete requests for the companies.
summary: Four gaps: no real-user evidence, version drift, groups served worse, and optimistic vignettes.
